haiku-low.q1: Nothing is signed in. No session is created; the user gets a second-step code form, backed by a pending_logins row and mfa_pending cookie.
haiku-low.q2: Only after a valid code from the new secret is confirmed (L4). A pending setup does not count as 2FA before then.
haiku-low.q3: Signs in and starts a session landing on /settings/security, showing N codes left and linking to setup. Sign-in does not depend on the notification email, which is queued after commit and never blocks.
haiku-low.q4: Five wrong entries, or 5 minutes from the password step. The pending row and cookie are cleared and the user is redirected to /login with 'Please sign in again'.
haiku-low.q5: All other sessions are deleted. The current session stays signed in.
haiku-low.q6: No. Codes at or below last_step are rejected, and same-code requests are serialized by a row lock. Drift tolerated is one 30-second step either side (T-1, T, T+1).
haiku-low.q7: In one transaction: upsert user_totp with the new secret and last_step, set confirmed_at, delete the enrollment, replace recovery codes with 10 new, delete other sessions and pending_logins. If it fails before commit, everything rolls back and the old state remains.
haiku-low.q8: Stored in the pending_logins table as sha256 of the mfa_pending cookie, which holds the raw token. Removed on success, on 5th wrong entry, after 5 minutes, on disable, or on confirm.
haiku-low.q9: Secret and last_step and confirmed_at are in user_totp; the pending secret is in totp_enrollments; recovery code hashes are in recovery_codes. 2FA is on exactly when a user_totp row exists.
haiku-low.q10: The old user_totp secret keeps protecting sign-in during replacement setup. If abandoned by cancel or 15-minute expiry, the enrollment is removed and the old secret stays.
haiku-low.q11: A 6-digit code is checked as an authenticator code; anything else is uppercased, stripped of spaces and hyphens, then checked as a recovery code. Wrong recovery codes count toward the 5-entry limit.
haiku-low.q12: NOT STATED as a path. The document says product has not decided or designed it; such a user cannot get past the second step.

sonnet.q1: Nothing but a second step: no session is created. A pending_logins row is inserted (older ones deleted), the mfa_pending cookie is set, and the code form is shown.
sonnet.q2: Only when the confirm step (L4) commits: user_totp is upserted with the new secret, and 2FA is on exactly when that row exists. A pending enrollment does not count; sign-in never reads totp_enrollments.
sonnet.q3: The recovery code is marked used via a conditional UPDATE, the remaining codes are counted, the pending_logins row is deleted, and after commit start_session(user_id, next="/settings/security") runs. The page says 'You used a recovery code, N left. Set up a new authenticator.' and links to L1. An email is queued with enqueue_email("recovery_code_used"). Sign-in does not depend on it: enqueue only queues, never blocks or fails the request, and is called after commit.
sonnet.q4: The 5th wrong entry, or 5 minutes passing since S4 (also a missing cookie or missing/expired row). The row is deleted, mfa_pending cleared, and the user is redirected to /login with 'Please sign in again' and starts again from the password.
sonnet.q5: At confirm (L4), every other session of the user is deleted; the current session (current sid) stays.
sonnet.q6: No. Only steps greater than last_step are accepted, and last_step is advanced on match, under a row lock (FOR UPDATE). Tolerance is one 30-second step either side (T-1, T, T+1), though steps at or below last_step are refused.
sonnet.q7: In one transaction: upsert user_totp with the pending secret, last_step set to matched step and confirmed_at; delete the enrollment row; delete old recovery codes and insert 10 new hashes; delete the user's other sessions; delete the user's pending_logins. If anything fails before commit, all rolls back: old secret, old codes and other sessions stay unchanged. Plaintext codes are shown only after commit.
sonnet.q8: Stored in the pending_logins table (token_hash sha256 PK, user_id, expires_at = created + 5 min, failures). The browser holds the mfa_pending cookie with the raw new_token(32) (httponly, secure, samesite=Lax, max_age=300, path=/login). It is removed on success (S7/S8), on the 5th wrong entry or expiry (S6), by a newer S4 sign-in for the same user, by L4 confirm or L6 disable, and by the periodic cleanup job (not relied on).
sonnet.q9: Secret: user_totp.secret_sealed (sealed with seal()). Enrolment status: totp_enrollments (secret_sealed, expires_at, one per user). Replay state: user_totp.last_step. Recovery codes: recovery_codes table (sha256 hashes, used_at). 2FA is on exactly when a user_totp row exists.
sonnet.q10: The old secret in user_totp is untouched and still used at sign-in; the new secret is only in totp_enrollments. If abandoned (cancel or 15 minutes pass), the enrollment is deleted or treated as missing and the account returns to On with the old secret kept.
sonnet.q11: A code of exactly 6 digits is checked as an authenticator code; anything else is uppercased, stripped of spaces and hyphens, and checked as a recovery code. Yes, an unknown or used recovery code is a wrong entry and increments failures, as do malformed codes, non-matching codes and replayed steps; 5 ends the attempt.
sonnet.q12: NOT STATED as a designed path. The document marks it open and undesigned (support reset undecided); such a user can get no further than S4. The only measure is a warning in the email and settings banner when 0 codes are left.
